Tabelog could NOT be read for this record and its menu page is unverified rather than empty: across 2026-09-01/02 it served a Cloudflare bot challenge ("Just a moment…") to curl and HTTP 403 to WebFetch, so nothing on it was ever observed. Its URL is deliberately absent from sources below because it was not read. Re-check it when Tabelog is reachable again — it may well carry a menu. That is the sixth unreadable menu in two shards, and this one is the most frustrating, because a chain this size almost certainly holds real allergen data internally. ⚠ WHY THIS RECORD IS WORTH HAVING EVEN EMPTY: a PREMIUM SALAD BAR is structurally one of the best formats in this entire dataset for a vegan, and among the better ones for a coeliac — raw vegetables and fruit carry no wheat and nothing animal, and unlike a set course you choose every component yourself. ⚠ AND WHY IT IS ALSO ONE OF THE RISKIEST: a buffet is SHARED TONGS. Croutons, pasta salad, dressings thickened with flour and a bread station all sit on the same counter, and a serving spoon moved between two trays undoes any amount of careful choosing. For a coeliac the bar is not "safe because it is vegetables"; it is safe only per-item and only if the tongs are. Sizzler is also known for its cheese toast, which is wheat. The chain ran an Aloha! Hawaiian Fair 15 July – 23 September 2026 with grilled items, coconut water and deli salads. Weekend morning salad bar 08:00–10:00 at selected branches; weekday lunch 11:00–15:00.

items.en: All-you-can-eat snow crab — the shop bills it as making the most of Hokkaido crab
items.note: Quoted 税抜 — BEFORE tax — so roughly ¥8,778 at the till. Steamed or boiled crab is one of the cleanest things a coeliac can eat: shellfish and water, with no coating and no marinade. What is not stated is what it is served WITH — ponzu is citrus plus SOY SAUCE, and a vinegared 三杯酢 normally contains soy too. Ask for lemon or salt. Crab rules out vegan.

tokyo_green_italian_torcia.price_note: ⚠ THIS RESTAURANT RUNS A VEGAN MENU AND MARKS ALLERGENS ON ITS PRINTED MENU — AND PUBLISHES NEITHER IN READABLE FORM. Both facts are worth having anyway, because they change how you'd approach the room. The shop states 「TORCIAはヴィーガンメニュー（植物性食材使用のメニュー）をさまざまなイタリアンに形を変えてご提供」 — a vegan menu carried across the Italian repertoire rather than one token dish — and frames the whole concept as 「あらゆる食の志向をもった人々が同じテーブルを囲んでお食事を楽しめる」, people with different diets sharing one table. On the menu pages it also states 「原材料に特定・推奨アレルギーが含まれる場合［ ］内に記載しています」: the STATUTORY AND RECOMMENDED ALLERGENS ARE PRINTED IN BRACKETS AGAINST EACH ITEM. That is rare in Tokyo and means the information a coeliac needs exists — on paper, in the restaurant. ⚠ AND THE CAVEAT THE SHOP VOLUNTEERS ITSELF: 「当店キッチンは動物性食材も取り扱っております」 — the kitchen handles animal ingredients, so the vegan menu is a recipe promise, not a separate kitchen. It also says to tell staff about allergies. WHY THERE IS ONLY ONE ITEM BELOW: every menu — dinner courses, à la carte, dolce, lunch, afternoon tea — is published as a JPG (lunch2.jpg … afternoon.jpg) with no text layer and no useful alt attributes, and Tabelog was unreadable. Tabelog could NOT be read for this record and its menu page is unverified rather than empty: across 2026-09-01/02 it served a Cloudflare bot challenge ("Just a moment…") to curl and HTTP 403 to WebFetch, so nothing on it was ever observed. Its URL is deliberately absent from sources below because it was not read. Re-check it when Tabelog is reachable again — it may well carry a menu. The single course price is the only figure stated in text anywhere. Lunch 11:00–15:00 (courses and pasta sets), 15:00–17:00 dolce sets and afternoon tea.

items.en: Dinner course, from — choose an antipasto and a pasta and combine as you like; the shop states a vegan version is available, and recommends wine pairing
items.note: The only price the site states in text (税込). Ask for the ヴィーガン course and read the brackets.

tokyo_hyotannabe_kaminarimon_t.price_note: Read from the restaurant's own menu page. No allergen statement anywhere. ⚠ ODEN IS A ONE-POT DISH AND THAT IS THE WHOLE ANSWER HERE. The shop names its broth — 「利尻昆布と鰹で引いたダシのきいたおでんスープ」, Rishiri kombu and bonito — so the pot is fish, and an oden pot is seasoned with soy sauce. Every one of the thirty-odd items below sits in that same broth, which means the daikon, the konnyaku, the potato, the tofu, the kelp and the yuba all arrive carrying fish stock and soy. There is no version of this menu where a vegan eats from the pot. ⚠⚠ AND THE ONE ITEM WORTH THE WHOLE RECORD: ちくわぶ, at ¥250, IS MADE OF WHEAT FLOUR. It is a 麩-family product — flour and water, kneaded and shaped into a tube — and it is a Kanto oden fixture that exists almost nowhere else. It is entirely plant-based and entirely wheat, the same trap as 車麩 at KiboKo: a vegan can eat it and a coeliac absolutely cannot, and nothing in the name warns you in either language. Set courses run 松 five items ¥1,450, 竹 eight ¥2,200, 梅 eleven ¥3,100, 桜 fifteen ¥4,450 — and a set removes the ability to choose which items, which for a coeliac means the ちくわぶ may simply arrive. The 鍋物 hotpots run October to March only.

items.note: A chosen-for-you set: 竹 eight items ¥2,200, 梅 eleven ¥3,100, 桜 fifteen ¥4,450. ⚠ For a coeliac a set is worse than à la carte here, because the ちくわぶ and the しゅうまい are both in the pot and neither is declined by ordering a number. THE POT DECIDES THIS, NOT THE INGREDIENT. The shop states its oden broth is 「利尻昆布と鰹で引いたダシ」 — Rishiri kelp AND BONITO — so every item simmering in it carries fish, and oden broth is seasoned with soy sauce as a matter of course. Everything in this section shares one pot, so a plant ingredient does not arrive as a plant dish.
Raw fish carries no wheat; the soy sauce it is dipped in does. Three-item version ¥3,800. Ask whether tamari is available.

The only plant item on this menu that does not go through the oden pot. Japanese pickles are often steeped in a soy or mirin brine and some are cured with bonito, so it is a question rather than an answer — but it is the one worth asking.

Raw cucumber with a miso dip — plant on both sides, and off the pot. The miso is the gluten question: Japanese miso is frequently 麦味噌, BARLEY, which is not on Japan's statutory allergen list and never appears on a label.

items.ja: ブロッコリー スナップエンドウ塩ゆで
items.note: Salt-boiled green vegetables and nothing else stated — the cleanest thing on this menu for both diets, and notably NOT cooked in the oden pot. Confirm it is boiled in its own water and served undressed.
Salt-fermented squid innards; commercial versions frequently add soy. 酒盗 also ¥550.
A commercial preparation of shark cartilage and umeboshi, normally seasoned with soy or mirin.
Grilled whole, normally just salted.
Dried ray fin, normally served with mayonnaise.
Ponzu is citrus plus SOY SAUCE and normally built on bonito dashi.
Dressing undeclared.
Bound with mayonnaise, which is egg.
The shop's named speciality, and deep-fried: a Japanese 揚げ is dredged in flour or starch, and this fryer also handles the karaage below.
Flour-dredged and soy-marinated. Octopus version ¥1,200.
The classic trap of tofu cookery: dusted in flour or starch, deep-fried, then sat in a dashi-and-soy broth — a dish made of soybean that arrives carrying both wheat and bonito.
Gyoza filling in a wing, and gyoza filling comes with its wrapper — plus a fried coating.
Simmered in soy and miso.
Simmered in a soy-and-mirin warishita.
Wonton wrappers are wheat.

Salt-grilled whole fish is one of the better things a coeliac can order in a Japanese izakaya — the fish is split, salted and grilled, with nothing battered or glazed. It is normally served with soy for the grated daikon, which is the part to decline.

items.en: Grilled chicken thigh with yuzu kosho
items.note: Yuzu kosho is yuzu peel, chilli and salt — no wheat in the condiment itself, which makes this more promising than a tare-glazed skewer. The marinade underneath is not stated.
Normally salt-grilled; undeclared.
Yaki onigiri is brushed with soy sauce as it grills — that crust is the soy.

items.ja: お茶漬け（梅・のり・明太子）
items.note: Ochazuke broth is dashi or a soy-based tsuyu, so it is a wheat route and a fish one at once. Beef tendon version ¥800.

items.en: The house hotpot, soy — October to March only
items.note: Named for its seasoning: 正油 IS soy sauce. Seasonal, October to March.

items.en: Chanko hotpot, salt — October to March only
items.note: The salt version is the one worth asking about: a 塩味 chanko is seasoned with salt rather than soy or miso, so the broth may be clean where the other two are not. Chanko stock is chicken or fish and the pot carries whatever goes in it, so this is a question rather than an answer — but it is the right question. Seasonal.

items.en: Michinoku hotpot, miso — October to March only
items.note: Miso is frequently 麦味噌, BARLEY, which Japanese allergen labelling does not cover. Seasonal.

tokyo_jikabaisen_ko_hi_bon_sel.price_note: ⚠ THE SHOP'S WEBSITE WAS NEVER FINISHED. cafebon.crayonsite.net loads, but its body reads 工事中 (under construction) and 準備中 (in preparation), and its only news item announces 「2017凡の新しいホームページ開設」 — a new homepage, announced in 2017 and still unbuilt nine years later. So there is no menu, no price and no dish name from the shop at any point. What the page does carry: the name 自家焙煎珈琲凡, the address 新宿3-23-1, ten seconds from the Shinjuku Alta entrance, a phone number, and a note that it closes at nine on Sundays and public holidays. Re-check when access returns. ⚠ ORIENTATION RATHER THAN FINDINGS, since nothing about this shop's own menu is sourced: 自家焙煎 means the shop roasts its own beans, and black coffee is roasted bean and water — no wheat, nothing animal — which makes the coffee itself one of the few things in this dataset that suits both diets by default. The two questions at any kissaten are the milk, and whether there is a cake or toast counter beside the roaster. Neither is answerable here.

tokyo_midtown_bbq_tokyo.price_note: No menu recorded. The page loads at 122KB but renders its content through JavaScript: nothing readable comes back as text, there is not a single 円 anywhere in the source, and the only structured data embedded in it is a list of EVENTS — St Patrick's Day 2026, 忘年会, 母の日, 飲み放題, Reservations — rather than any dish or price. Tabelog could not be checked at all: as of 2026-09-02 it returns HTTP 403 with a 5,812-byte Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its menu page for this shop is UNVERIFIED rather than empty and its URL is deliberately absent from sources. Re-check when access returns. ⚠ ORIENTATION RATHER THAN FINDINGS, offered because the category is unusually clear-cut and none of it is sourced for this restaurant: American barbecue is one of the better cuisines for a coeliac in principle, because smoked meat is meat, salt, pepper and smoke — the rub and the smoke add nothing. What ruins it is almost always the SAUCE and the SIDES. Barbecue sauce is normally built on Worcestershire or soy, both wheat routes, and in Japan a house BBQ sauce very often uses 醤油 outright. The sides are the other half: cornbread, mac and cheese, buns and fried pickles are wheat, and a bun arrives with the meat unless you say otherwise. So the shape of the question at any BBQ counter is "can I have it dry-rubbed, sauce on the side, no bun" — but whether this kitchen can answer yes is not established here. Nothing suits a vegan at a smokehouse without asking.

tokyo_shoya_suidobashi_honke_t.price_note: No dish or price recorded, and the chain menu was chased to the end before giving up. 庄や is a Daisyo chain, and Daisyo does publish a grand menu — regionally, with 首都圏 (syouya_B) being the one that covers Suidobashi. That menu resolves to a 2.3MB PDF with NO TEXT LAYER: zero characters extract from it. The corporate site has no allergen page at all (/allergy/ is a 404), which is worth noting for a chain of this size. Tabelog could not be checked: as of 2026-09-02 it returns HTTP 403 with a 5,812-byte Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its page for this shop is UNVERIFIED rather than empty and its URL is deliberately absent from sources. Re-check when access returns. ⚠ WHAT IS READABLE, AND IT IS USEFUL EVEN WITHOUT DISHES: the metropolitan menu's own section headings come through as text, and they map the board — 豪快刺身盛り, 特選刺身, 煮込み/珍味/サラダ, 焼きとり, 逸品料理, 揚げもの, あて巻寿司/めし処, 甘味, then 生ビール, サワー, ハイボール/焼酎, 日本酒, ワイン/果実酒/ソフトドリンク. For a coeliac that tells you where the shop concentrates: the 刺身 sections are raw fish limited only by the soy sauce, 焼きとり turns on タレ versus 塩, and 揚げもの and 巻寿司 are settled against. For a vegan there is nothing — this is a fish izakaya whose own description leads on 新鮮な魚料理. The shop is also known for an あさりバター, which is dairy.

tokyo_chompoo.price_note: No menu published anywhere readable. The record's stored website is the Shibuya PARCO tenant page, which carries the concept, the phone number and the hours but not one dish or price; the only link it gives for the restaurant itself is an Instagram account, which is not a menu this dataset can cite, and there is no standalone site. Tabelog could not be checked: as of 2026-09-02 it returns HTTP 403 with a 5,812-byte Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its page for this shop is UNVERIFIED rather than empty and its URL is deliberately absent from sources. Re-check when access returns. ⚠ WHAT THE PARCO PAGE DOES ESTABLISH, and it shapes the question worth asking: the kitchen is presented as herb-led rather than heat-led — Thai food that is 「辛いだけではない」, built on fresh herbs — under a chef who trained across Southeast Asian cooking before specialising. That matters because the herb-and-citrus side of Thai cooking (larb, yam salads, som tam) is where the wheat-free dishes live, while the heat-led side leans on nam prik pao and oyster sauce. ⚠ AND THE STANDING THAI CAVEATS, recorded here as orientation rather than as findings about this kitchen: Thai food is largely RICE-based, so a coeliac usually has more to work with than at most restaurants — the wheat concentrates in the fried section, in OYSTER SAUCE, and in the egg noodles (バーミー, カオソーイ) that sit beside the rice ones. A vegan has the harder time, because fish sauce and shrimp paste are foundational. 4F Shibuya PARCO, 11:30–22:30, last orders 21:30; takeaway and Wolt delivery.

tokyo_tachigui_soba_kamu_stand.price_note: No menu found, and this one is an honest empty rather than an unchecked one. The shop has no site of its own — the record's stored website is a Tabelog listing — and its Retty menu page was read directly and is explicitly empty: 料理がありません, コースがありません, ランチがありません, ドリンクがありません, テイクアウトメニューがありません, with Retty's own caveat that what it shows reflects the time of a review rather than the current board. So a menu source was read and it genuinely holds nothing, which is different from the Tabelog situation. Tabelog could not be checked: as of 2026-09-02 it returns HTTP 403 with a 5,812-byte Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its page for this shop is UNVERIFIED rather than empty and its URL is deliberately absent from sources. Re-check when access returns. ⚠ THE QUESTION A STANDING SOBA SHOP RAISES, offered as orientation since nothing about this kitchen is sourced: Japanese soba is normally 二八 — 80% buckwheat to 20% WHEAT — and the ratio is almost never published. Even a 十割 kitchen dusts its boards with 打ち粉, usually wheat flour, and a standing shop boils every order in one pot of shared water all day, which is the strongest version of that problem in this dataset. The tsuyu is soy and bonito, so it is a wheat route and a vegan one at once. A 立ち食い counter also has no room to keep anything separate and no time to answer questions at the rush.
